title: Connect Codex materialization to native proposal review

requirement.summary: Add a capability-gated Codex MCP tool that accepts only a normalized low-risk task draft, presents the exact proposal through native form elicitation, and creates it only after the human explicitly admits that exact preview.

objective.rationale: The reference proposal seam is complete, and the product owner selected its next connection to the current Codex host and a native review surface.

goal: Extend the foreground Codex MCP Adapter so the current Agent materializes normalized proposal fields and one capability-negotiated native form records the human review before exclusive task creation.
non_goals: Do not add an OpenAI API call, API key, second model, external service, custom App Server client, web component, or another host.
Do not send raw prompts, transcripts, source content, credentials, absolute host paths, proposal IDs, authority flags, or human decisions through model-authored tool input.
Do not treat MCP tool permission, model intent, form display, action=accept alone, standing policy, or terminal presence as admission of the proposed task.
Do not admit non-low-risk tasks, start a session, implement the generated task, expand scope, grant an exception, or authorize Git, publication, release, deployment, or external writes.
Do not install the changed package, modify the existing local Codex config, run an external replay, touch NYC, commit, or push.
acceptance_signals: The existing five read-only governance tools remain unchanged, while the proposal-review tool is listed only for clients that declare MCP form elicitation support.

The current Coding Agent supplies only strict normalized low-risk task meaning; Adapter-owned repository identity, proposal identity, privacy, authority, preview digests, and decision binding cannot be model-authored.
The Adapter emits one bounded elicitation/create form containing the exact reviewed plan and one admit/change/reject decision, and binds the response to the pending tool call and elicitation ID.

Only action=accept plus the exact admit decision can revalidate and exclusively create the reviewed task; decline, cancel, change, reject, malformed, stale, raced, unsupported, interrupted, and EOF paths write nothing.
The result distinguishes factual repository mutation from denied downstream authority and reports zero AgentGov model/network calls and no Core receipt of raw conversation.
The packaged Codex config enables the new tool without claiming that ordinary tool permission is governance admission; existing custom config remains create-missing-only and is not overwritten.
Focused protocol/proposal/config tests, task/scope/repository governance, documentation checks, the complete supported-Python suite, and diff checks pass.

items: A bidirectional STDIO implementation could misbind an elicitation response or deadlock the foreground tool call.
Generic MCP tool permission could be confused with the distinct human task-admission decision.
A malformed, cancelled, or raced review could create a task the human did not review unless validation remains atomic through the final write.
The current Codex UI may add another permission interruption or render the bounded preview poorly; fixture tests cannot establish live usability.
Existing uncommitted Adapter 1.2.4 and reference proposal work share the working copy and must remain distinguishable.

stop_conditions: Stop if the client does not explicitly advertise form elicitation or if a response cannot be bound to the exact pending request.
Stop if any non-admit, malformed, interrupted, or failed path can mutate the repository or advance task state.
Stop if the change requires raw conversation in Core, a new credential/model/network service, weakened proposal validation, hidden configuration overwrite, or expanded project authority.
Stop before installation, local config mutation, external replay, NYC work, Git writes, publication, release, or deployment.

decision.rationale: The product owner selected Codex production materialization and native proposal review on 2026-08-07; ADR-0015 maps native review to capability-negotiated MCP form elicitation.
